1.
A perusal of Annexure No. CA-1 to the counter affidavit filed by the State today, which is taken on record, indicates that service of notice upon respondent no.2/informant(victim) is sufficient.

Today,
when the case was called out, no one has appeared on behalf of the respondent no.2.

However,
learned A.G.A. for the State is present.
In such circumstances, this Court proceeded to hear the appeal on merits.

sentences.text: While pressing the present appeal, counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has not committed any crime as indicated in the F.I.R. lodged on 05.09.2023, in which the victim, who is an adult, alleged that on 04.09.2023, the appellant committed rape with her in his house.

4. He also submitted that medical opinion does not support the story of the prosecution as no external or internal injury was found by the doctor concerned while examining the informant/victim, despite the fact that the victim was examined on 06.09.2023.
5.

He further submitted that the victim in her statements recorded under Section 161 & 164 CrPC supported the story of prosecution, however, the story of prosecution in F.I.R. and the statements of the victim are completely false for the reasons that in the F.I.R., the victim says that she is 18 years old whereas according to the mark-sheet of class 8, she is about 22 years old and commission of offence of the alleged crime by the appellant in his house, where entire family of the appellant resides, is impossible.
It appears that on account of village party-bandi, the appellant has been implicated in the present case by the victim.

6. He lastly submitted that taking note of the aforesaid facts, particularly the fact that to support the story of prosecution, there is no medical evidence, as also that the appellant has no previous criminal history and is languishing in jail since 09.09.2023, the appeal is liable allowed, the order impugned is liable to be set aside and the appellant is entitled to be released on bail.
7.
Learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail, however, he could not dispute the aforesaid contention of counsel for the appellant 8.

Considered the submissions advanced by the counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State and all the relevant documents placed on record.
9.

Upon due consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions of counsel for the appellant and learned A.G.A., including the statements of the victim recorded under Section 161 and 164 CrPC, as also that to support the story of prosecution, there is no medical evidence, as also the fact that the appellant has no previous criminal history and is languishing in jail since 09.09.2023,
this Court finds that the present appeal is liable to be allowed.
Accordingly, it is allowed.

10. Order dated 06.11.2023, passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Lakhimpur Kheri, in Bail Application No. 552 of 2023, Computerized Case No. 3801/2023 CNRUPLP01007752 2023 (Vipin vs. State of U.P.) in Special Case No. 324 of 2023, arising out of F.I.R/ Case Crime No. 0240 of 2023, under Sections 376, 342 I.P.C., and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, Police Station- Uchauliya,
District- Lakhimpur Kheri, is hereby set aside.
11.

2 sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following additional conditions :-
(i) The appellant shall cooperate with the prosecution during trial.
(ii) The appellant shall not tamper with the evidence during trial.

(iii) The appellant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness(s).
(iv) The appellant shall not commit an offence.

(v) The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

(vi) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through counsel.
(vii) The appellant shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
(viii) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
12.
In case of default of above conditions, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law 13.

As this order relates to enlargement of the appellant on bail, it is clarified that observation(s)
made in this order shall have no bearing on the merits of the case and the trial court shall not be influenced by any observation(s) made in this order.
